items.text: Thank you for all your precious feedback, bug reports, and insight! We're constantly working on improving the game - doing not just bug fixes, but also rebalancing and quality-of-life changes too.
Our second update is finally here, with plenty of killed bugs, fixed softlock issues, re-balancing changes, and new features.
You can use the save and exit feature in 1999 and Russ Kurtell modes without needing to check the "protected quicksaves" checkbox.
From now on, you can have 3 auto-saves and 3 quick saves instead of the previous 2. This gives you a total of 6 saves, if you also use the “protected quicksaves” feature.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/6073e33bf5c4f0cc882c12cf7438fb9aa8c8f9a5.jpg"]

We fixed the "Dahlia vs Machine Brain" softlock issue that caused progression blocks for several players. This also retroactively fixes the progression for those who got stuck there - you don't have to start a new game.
For some players the Secret Weapon either dissapeared or never appeared in the first place after saving and loading during the last phase of Marco's quest. It is fixed now.

The 1999 and Russ Kurtell modes were a bit too easy for huge majority of the players. We adjusted some of it's values to be a bit harder, but not too much that it's altering the core experience in a fundametal way.
The prices were too low and enemy loot was too generous on the two highest difficulities. This was also adjusted a bit.
Bosses - the 3 main bosses were a bit too easy on every difficulity (even on the normal "classic horror" mode), we give them approx 20% more HP. (But all their other values remained the same!)
These changes won't affect the secret boss.
Note: You don't need to start a new game for any of these changes, you can continue playing the game without problems.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/a0117524665a29b5097f6b2bba145c9f4b5880af.jpg"]
There was another duplicated audio log (history lesson 1), so we deleted the wrong one.
We put an extra flare gun to the janitors haven, and one to the Borealis Gardens - dark timeline. (there was only 2 before in the entire game)
The alarm sound at the start of the game is now less loud.
We further tweaked the flashlight, so it is stronger and brighter now, without being too overwhelming.
We also fixed a lot of smaller issues, some are graphical, others are feature or progression related.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/d938f1eb366e485ab0d1b9462cee4c293439334f.jpg"]

We are constanlty updating the performance of the game and did a minor performance update in this patch too, but don't expect huge changes yet, the big performance update is the next on our list. (see roadmap below...)

The Deck now has a 30 FPS lock function the player can activate or deactivate from the menu. This is so that we can achieve consistent and steady performance without overheating the deck. More significant optimalizations and consistently higher frame rate is also on their way, so stay tuned for more!

Our third update will focus on optimalization on every platform, so both PC and SteamDeck players can expect significant leaps in performance soon. In addition, we will, of course, continue fixing other bugs, and you can also expect some minor quality-of-life changes.
Our fourth update will be a bigger one, in this, expect significant quality-of-life updates, new features, new difficulty, refined gunplay, inventory and map updates, and many-many more.
Stay tuned, and stay groovy, Janitors! Keep up the good work, send us bug reports, your ideas, insights, and suggestions - without your support and dedication, we won't be here!
So thank you for that!
The Team

notes.title: Check out the changelog for the first batch of fixes - build: 6508

items.text: Ladders

The handling of ladders has undergone a major overhaul. Climbing ladders isn’t as insanely fast anymore, making them way easier to navigate, and we’ve also increased the ladders’ collision boxes, giving them a bit of “coyote time,” so it’s much harder to fall off them.
Note for the players: At the end of the ladder, no need to jump. Just go upward and you'll automatically climb up. If you press an extra jump, the player will push off the ladder.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/c30443416daf5d5e28d723c7f13a63493b44e774.jpg"]
Fall damage

If you did fall... We've fine-tuned the fall damage too, so even if you fall from a ladder (or from any kind of hight) you now have to fall from much greater heights to suffer serious injury or even die.
Charley (Mild Spoilers)
Charley is fixed and tamed now. He no longer can cause a softlock, his quest is updating no matter how you finish him, and some of its values have also been changed.
Charley can't go near to the Heal-O-Dome stations, so he can't cause a death-loop there.

Charley's health has been significantly nerfed. WARNING! He's still by far the strongest boss in the game, but now he can be defeated even without performing the secret ritual - as long as you're careful and resourceful.
Charley's attacks are a little more forgiving.
We've also reduced Charley's speed a bit, but his long-range jumps are still dangerous.
In addition, we fixed the bug that prevented Charley's quest from being completed unless it was finished with "the ritual".
Save system
The save system has also been revamped. From now on, the game will always make an auto save in the Janitors' Haven hallway, and we've also added a “Save and Exit” feature to the in-game menu.
You can still exit the game without saving if you want, but now you have the option to save whenever you leave the game.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/1764a92207eae8896ddf32543fe3455efbed95a9.jpg"]
Mutamod UI overlap
There was a nasty UI overlap if you purchased a lot of Mutamod upgrades in Dr. Miriam's Mutamod vending machine. (especially level 2 and level 3 ones) It is fixed now.
New PDA in stasis

We put a PDA (PHCD) in the very first area of the game (Stasis Section), beside the first audio log you encounter. Now you can immediately check your stuff - like the transcripts of the audio logs, objectives, etc.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/de900fcee9426bfd5f98318644a97d9f585ad53c.jpg"]
Luxury code
We fixed the server override code in the Luxury Section. Now if you pair the letters with the numbers in the correct order, you can override the system and no need to brute-force the solution.
Duplicated log
There was a duplicated auido log (History lesson 2), now it can be found only in one place instead of two.
Achievement description fix
One of the achievement descriptions (Warren Wrenchman) was misleading, so we corrected the wording of it.

notes.title: This was just the first update, expect more in the near future!

items.text: We are now working on edge-case softlock issues and a lot of quality of life changes and performance fixes. Please keep the feedback coming, our to-do list grew quite a bit because of your ideas and suggestions. We'll continue to work on further improoving the game.
If you encouner any problems, reach out for us either in the Steam discussions, or on our Discord server. We are really active and checking the messages in an hourly basis.
Keep on groovin', Janitors! - The Team.
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2067820/RetroSpace/"]

First of all, thank you to everyone who’s playing the game and sharing their feedback. A super friendly, dedicated, and close-knit community is beginning to form, and we’re incredibly grateful for that!

notes.title: List of the most notable features and changes

items.text: Save system update (protected quick save feature).
Ui system upcade (not floaty, fixed).
Box stacking and item handling update.
Wrench update - more range, more damage, a new charged attack!
Gunplay update #1 - already loaded guns, enhanched sounds, more damage and improoved fire-rate for the shotgun and the smallgun.
"Silence the discord!" - less chaos and cacophony on the audio front.
Hello darkness update - the game is less dark, even if we are not using the flashlight.
Turret damage visibility - The turret will emit smoke and sparks if it's damaged.
Player movement and mantling tweaks
Rhino mutamod update - Now it's obvious that the effect is on if we are using melee weapons.
Enemy state on-off - you can turn the enemy state indicator on and off anytime from the menu.
Cloning error update - tweaked the entire system, as well as the effects of certain errors.
Using the PDA and the inventory while crouching
Visibility and player guidence - there were some new player guidence tweaks added to "timelline B" to help the players get around without being handholdy.
A ton of bugfixes and tweaks - both visual and functional.

An extra button has been added to the difficulty selection screen (and to the menu as well) that allows you to enable "protected quicksaves." This means that when this feature is enabled, your quicksave won’t be overwritten even if your in-game character dies, and you can easily load your previous save without any penalties. This is, of course, entirely optional, but you can turn it on or off at any time.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/f7f32f3dd8dc8beb0c7c1350320db487a97a36cc.jpg"]
The previous, rather clunky, floaty, and janky "interactable UI" has been replaced by a much more elegant, attractive, and user-friendly fixed version.

notes.title: - Box stacking and item handling update

items.text: We've greatly improved the way objects are moved, stacked, thrown, and handled in general. It’s now much easier to use this feature; if an object gets too close to you, it becomes transparent so it doesn’t interfere with your view, and stacking them, or building “box stairs” so to speak, has become much smoother and more fun.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/c8bbadc9a5789043d1fb456c57f8c0a11edbc513.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/c5b7da978aefd098296d35bcceb754bba60d6df0.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/fc26795c9da0e4a5d3756db2559b0f8d4a3a84a6.jpg"]

The wrench was a favorite weapon for many of you, but you were a bit dissatisfied with its power. We’ve increased the damage slightly (not too much, so not to break the balance), extended it's range a bit (so you can hit headcreeps even while standing), and added a secondary attack mode as well.

Now holding down the right mouse button initiates a charging attack; if you release it once it’s fully charged, you’ll deal multiple times the damage. When launched from a good position (with some skill or luck), this can be extremely devastating and can even result in an instant kill attack.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/c65519a0b5fe131e4572cd53c32d8e53a53fa82f.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/cf35b4e5c5560adffaeaebfefc9c5887698bb0e1.jpg"]

We’re constantly working on the gunplay, and we’ve made a bunch of tweaks to it in this first round. We’ve increased the base pistol rate of fire and the bullet ricochet effect. We’ve also tweaked the animations and the weapon shake. We’ve even changed the sound effects to make it a bit more impactful, even though this pistol is intentionally designed to be a weaker starter weapon.
The shotgun has also received some tweaks, new sounds, and its rate of fire has been increased slightly to make it feel a little less sluggish - though we were very careful to maintain balance here.

In addition, we’ve tweaked the explosions: if enemies are close enough to the epicenter of an explosion, they won’t just die - they’ll be blown to pieces. (GIBS!) This is incredibly satisfying, but be careful! In this case, the bodies won’t be lootable. (Instead, you can throw the limbs and heads around.)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/2e230dd125dd39950e480d64eff979a17970d434.jpg"]

Certain sounds were too loud, so in some places the audio overlapping sounds could result in a kind of cacophony. We’ve made significant improvements in this area, and we’re currently working on a system that will mute certain channels while more important sounds are playing (for example, an important story monologue).
Darkness is good; darkness is our friend. Especially in a game like this. However, as many have rightly pointed out, it was so dark in some places that it led to complete disorientation.

We’ve fixed this as well; now, even in the darkest places, you can faintly make out the outlines of the environment, making it much easier to find your way around—even without using a flashlight—without having to compromise the atmosphere.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/4bbfc0d7338a7340ef53ed8bc199d8eb42501fef.jpg"]
From now on, when we damage the turret, we'll see it smoking and sparking. This makes it clear that we're actually damaging it and that it isn't immune to our attacks.

We've tweaked the player movement and the mantling system, making them much easier and smoother to use. Now it's much easier to catch ledges and edges without the system feeling too automated. Overall, this has greatly improved the feel of character movement in the game.

It wasn't clear to many players that the Rhyno body Mutamod (passive), once purchased and equipped, only activates when you're holding a melee weapon. We've now made this clear in the Mutamod menu. In addition, the ability now provides a slightly higher damage bonus than before.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/b27662c94c08e29158bc3405c74c8bba7d12315b.jpg"]

Some of you were bothered by the indicator that appears above enemies' heads, which shows whether they are in a peaceful, scouting, or attacking state. You can now turn this on or off at any time in the menu.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/288810f25c6498aa3b8d2d0fe0e530823966a966.jpg"]

Certain cloning errors were occurring too frequently and had too strong an effect. We've now thoroughly reworked and tweaked them (I'm looking at you, alcoholism!) to achieve a much more balanced experience.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/47e9dc9bad11594c1de7086797a531a6ce1e74d5.jpg"]

notes.title: - Using the PDA and the inventory while crouching

items.text: Until now, we could only do these things while standing, and if we were crouching, using them would make us stand up. That has now changed; both the PDA and the Inventory can be used while crouching. If the Janitor's knees can handle it, why not?

Without coming across as overly patronizing or spoon-feeding the player, at a certain point in the demo (during that specific B-timeline segment), we made it a little clearer what to do and where to go. We did this without any tutorial pop-ups, or anything "agressive" like that, simply by refining the objective description, and using some visual cues.

notes.title: - A ton of bugfixes and tweaks

items.text: In addition to all of this, we’ve fixed more than 100 various minor functional or visual bugs.
Issues may still occur, since the game is still very much in active development, but we believe this update has taken the RetroSpace experience to a whole new level. :)

notes.title: Thank you again for all your feedback and support!

items.text: We hope you'll have a blast playing the demo.

notes.title: Keep on groovin', Cosmic Janitors! - The RetroSpace Team

notes.title: Thank you for all the feedback, and, of course, the nice reviews. Since the demo was released, the team has been working on the project with even greater dedication - and we’re pleased to bring you the first demo update

items.text: While we want to preserve the game’s hardcore and survival horror elements, we’d also like to give players more room to experiment. After all, it’s one of the key elements of any immersive sim. So, in the event of death, we only have to return to our corpse to extract our genes (if we want to get rid of the cloning error), but from now on we won’t lose items from our inventory - at least not on this (medium) difficulty level, which is playable in the demo.

Bodies left behind: We noticed that bodies sometimes end up in the wrong place or even disappear. We've improved this system, so now it's much less likely that your body will vanish or end up in an inaccessible location. It still can happen rarely, in very specific cases, so we'll tweak this system further.

Some users encountered a black screen when starting a new game, and it wouldn't go away. Although we couldn't reproduce this issue internally, we were able to resolve it with the help of a few helpful players. (thanks again, guys!) In theory, this shouldn't happen anymore after the update.

Two cloning errors proved to be a bit more annoying than we had expected: “alcoholism” and “bad manners.” We refined both; their mechanics remain largely the same, but their effects occur much less frequently.

The enemies are intentionally extremely tough; that’s part of the game’s core loop. But we’ve noticed ourselves that if the opponents needed just one or two fewer shots or hits to be defeated, it would provide a much more balanced experience. (especially on a medium difficulity) So, without taking away the hardcore edge of the game or nerf the enemies, we made the weapons a little bit more powerful.

Again, the game is dark for a reason, but some of you understandably stated that the game can be too dark, especially in the second part of the demo. Without altering the game's atmosphere, we've managed to significantly improve this by adding a few extra light sources here and there, and making the flashlight brighter and able to shine further.

Mantling (ledge grabbing): The ledge grabbing aka mantling mechanic needed a little extra work. Now it's easier to handle, you can now use it in tighter spaces, and you can even climb into vents with it.: ##

New shortcut: In the second half of the demo - after "thath thing" happened, there is a new shortcut and traversal option open to give even more opportunities for the players to explore and experiment. Also, this will help find something in the end of the demo, which may have caused some people a bit of a headache. (without holding the player's hand!)
You can now use the PDA - aka "PHCD" - even while crouching, so it's much more stealth-friendly and won't snap you out of your current state.
We've managed to significantly reduce loading times. This mainly affects slightly less powerful machines, but even those with more advanced hardware will notice the difference.
We fixed a few text and/or localization errors. (For example, in one place we accidentally referred to Professor Hammond as "Dr. Hammond")
...and a bunch of smaller bugs were also fixed!
Be sure to update your build, the new versions's build number is 5855 which you can find on the main menu, in the bottom left corner of the screen.
We’ve taken note of many of your suggestions and are already hard at work on them, so you can expect the game to continue evolving in the near future.
So expect: further balancing, tweaked mutamods, more bugfixes and tweaks, and more performance updates!
Thank you once again for your feedback, comments, and ideas. It means a lot to us, and we’re doing our best to meet everyone’s needs while staying true to the game’s original vision.
See you soon! - The Team
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/ea7423d26fb6095bb3d1e5244d64f123f0596786.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43467429/35f7d398a0fff1fde3cf86d33c03bab396ca8d69.png"]
Hey, Janitors!
Thanks for all the feedback! We knew we’d hear a wide range of reactions, which is why it was a good idea to share the demo with you as soon as possible. We’re listening to what you have to say!

A major update is coming soon, which will improve many systems based on your feedback. Perhaps the most important of these will be balancing the death-rebirth system, as many of you wrote that you find it too unfair or hardcore, or perhaps difficult to understand. We’re already working on this around the clock, so expect an update within a few days.

We try to respond to every single piece of feedback individually, but please bear with us if it takes a while, as we have a lot to go through. Rest assured, we read and take note of everything! But really, thank you for all the kind words, feedback, ideas and player stories you shared with us - it means a lot, and motivates us to work even harder!
Stay tuned, play more, be funky!
The Team
